title: NULL Functions, String Concatenation and Pagination Differences
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of COALESCE and recognize product-specific NULL replacement functions.
Compare IFNULL, ISNULL and NVL at a conceptual level.
Use SQLite's || operator for string concatenation.
Recognize product differences in string concatenation and NULL behaviour.
Apply LIMIT/OFFSET pagination with a deterministic ORDER BY.

understand.concept: NULL handling, string concatenation and row limiting syntax vary across database products. COALESCE is widely supported, while IFNULL, ISNULL and NVL are product-specific. SQLite uses || for concatenation and LIMIT/OFFSET for pagination; other products provide different alternatives.
understand.whyItMatters: These differences commonly break migrations and application queries even when the underlying data model is similar.
understand.analogy: SQL portability is like translating a precise instruction into several product dialects: the intent stays the same, but the exact words and rules can differ.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not model type systems, function return types, time-zone rules, optimizer behaviour or transaction semantics.

explain.narrative:
## NULL replacement functions
COALESCE returns the first non-NULL expression and is widely supported. SQLite and MySQL support IFNULL in their dialects; SQL Server uses ISNULL; Oracle uses NVL. Return type and conversion rules can differ.

## String concatenation
SQLite and PostgreSQL commonly use ||. MySQL supports CONCAT and SQL Server commonly uses CONCAT. NULL behaviour and type conversion can differ among products.

## Pagination
SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL support LIMIT/OFFSET. SQL Server supports TOP and OFFSET/FETCH patterns. Standard FETCH FIRST syntax is supported by several engines. Always use a deterministic ORDER BY before applying pagination.

### String and NULL portability
COALESCE is widely supported, but IFNULL, ISNULL and NVL are vendor-specific. Concatenation operators and NULL propagation differ. Test NULL input cases explicitly and choose a fallback only when it has a valid business meaning.

### Pagination portability
LIMIT/OFFSET is common in SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL; SQL Server supports TOP and OFFSET/FETCH; several engines support FETCH FIRST. Always use a stable ORDER BY with a unique tie-breaker for repeatable pages. Large offsets can become expensive; keyset pagination may be preferable for deep navigation.

examples.title: Use COALESCE for a NULL fallback
examples.explanation: Uses COALESCE to substitute a label when the first expression is NULL. COALESCE is broadly supported; the result type is determined according to each engine's type-resolution rules.

examples.title: Concatenate values with SQLite's operator
examples.explanation: Uses SQLite's || operator to concatenate two text values. PostgreSQL and several other engines also use ||, while MySQL commonly uses CONCAT; SQL Server behaviour depends on the operator and settings.

examples.title: Use IFNULL in SQLite
examples.explanation: Uses SQLite's IFNULL function to return the fallback text when the first argument is NULL. IFNULL is not universal SQL syntax; SQL Server uses ISNULL and Oracle uses NVL, with product-specific return-type behaviour.

examples.title: Apply deterministic pagination
examples.code: SELECT value FROM (SELECT 10 AS value UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 40) AS values_table ORDER BY value LIMIT 2 OFFSET 1;
examples.explanation: Orders the derived values before applying LIMIT and OFFSET. The ORDER BY is essential because pagination without a deterministic order can return overlapping or inconsistent pages as data changes.

examples.title: Use a fallback and concatenate a nullable field
examples.explanation: Combines COALESCE with concatenation so a NULL input becomes the label Guest before the suffix is appended. Without the fallback, concatenation with NULL can produce NULL depending on the engine and operator.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples and identify which syntax is SQLite-specific and which NULL fallback function is broadly portable.
practise.independentTask: Rewrite a report query for SQLite, MySQL and SQL Server. Compare NULL fallback, string concatenation and pagination syntax, and include a stable ordering column.
hints: COALESCE is widely supported for NULL fallback.
IFNULL, ISNULL and NVL are product-specific alternatives.
Pagination syntax differs; SQL Server commonly uses OFFSET/FETCH or TOP.
Always use ORDER BY before pagination to make page contents deterministic.

questions.prompt: Which NULL function is widely supported across SQL products?
questions.explanation: COALESCE is a broadly supported standard expression.

questions.prompt: Which function is commonly associated with SQL Server?
questions.explanation: SQL Server uses ISNULL for a NULL replacement expression.

questions.prompt: Which operator does SQLite commonly use for string concatenation?
questions.explanation: SQLite uses the || operator to concatenate strings.

questions.prompt: Which syntax is commonly used by SQL Server for pagination?
questions.explanation: SQL Server commonly uses TOP or OFFSET/FETCH patterns.

questions.prompt: Why should pagination include ORDER BY?
options: To make the selected page deterministic
questions.answer: To make the selected page deterministic
questions.explanation: Without a stable order, page membership is not reliably defined.
